title: State And Status Visibility Design
excerpt: State and status visibility design makes system, process, device, transaction, commitment, information, and evidence states legible at the moment users need to act. The capability covers state hierarchy, aggregation, layout stability, recognition over recall, status taxonomies, and evidence-calibrated display decisions.
metaDescription: Documentation of state visibility design for complex interfaces, including hierarchy, aggregation, transaction state, evidence state, and limits.
summary: State and status visibility design is the capability of making operational state legible without forcing users to infer it from symptoms, scattered indicators, raw alarms, or ambiguous values. The documented evidence spans maritime, medical, industrial, residential energy, space, command, radio, and traffic-monitoring interfaces, with different evidence strength for each engagement.
definition: State and status visibility design is the design of interface structures that make the current condition of a system, process, device, transaction, command, datum, or evidence relationship understandable at the point of action, with the status class and evidence basis kept explicit.
keyFacts: State visibility concerns what the machine is doing; information state concerns what is known about a reading and how well it is known.

Core mechanisms include state hierarchy, state aggregation, layout stability, recognition over recall, process mimics, sensor-cadence synchronisation, redundant non-colour cues, and explicit status taxonomies.

In the Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement, energy state identification was 50% faster in a controlled environment experiment with 24 subjects; glance reduction during manoeuvres was measured by eye tracking with 7 subjects during sea trials.
In the Gericke industrial HMI engagement, client-measured fault-diagnosis time fell by roughly two-thirds at three sites, and repeat alarms more than halved within a confirmed single-variable window.

In the Kardion MCS Controller engagement, the layout stability standard required no element to shift position across any view transition; the submitted design passed FDA evaluation with no design changes required.

The deSoutter Medical / Zethon engagement used redundant spatial, icon, and colour cues because colour alone was unreliable under operating theatre conditions; 8 surgeons reported brief-glance recognition in structured review sessions.
KISPE Space concerns information state, not device or process state, and remained a specification reasoned from a synthetic fixture without executed validation.
Schone Airspace Group Mission Control adds transaction state: the condition of an instruction in flight between request and observed result.
Raymarine adds the requested-versus-effective distinction, where the operative value remains visible when a requested value is blocked or superseded by protocol behaviour.
The maritime traffic software portfolio adds evidence state, including source, observation time, receipt time, association status, and the refusal to display an uncalibrated confidence score.
bodyMarkdown:
## Summary

Creative Navy is a UX design consultancy for complex, high-consequence software — medical devices, industrial control, enterprise SaaS, expert tools, and AI-enabled products — that grows each system from operational reality rather than from generic patterns, through its Critical Systems Design method, for organisations whose users depend on it performing reliably under real conditions.

State and status visibility design makes the condition of a system understandable at the point where a user needs to act. In Creative Navy's documentation, state visibility concerns what the machine is doing; information state concerns what is known about a reading and how well it is known.

State visibility is not the same as showing more data. A display can expose many symptoms while still failing to communicate the state that produced them. The Gericke industrial HMI engagement illustrates this distinction: the legacy Easydos Pro interface exposed alarm lists, raw error codes, and scattered parameters, while the redesigned process mimic showed the physical process and highlighted failed components directly on the diagram.

State visibility also includes the behaviour of transitions. A state indicator must communicate the current state, the change from one state to another, and the evidence that supports the displayed state. Mode changes, command transitions, sensor-cadence differences, and asynchronous work all create state-visibility risk when the interface visually replaces a confirmed state with a requested or inferred one.

## Domain vocabulary for state and status visibility

System state, operational state, and device state refer to the current condition of the system as relevant to the user's next action.

State visibility is the degree to which users can understand what the system is doing without active interpretation.

Glance readability and peripheral attention describe state communication that remains usable under brief, partial attention. The user should not have to stop and read when the operating context requires ambient awareness.

Recognition over recall means that the user recognises the state from visual pattern rather than remembering what an indicator means. In high-consequence contexts, this is treated as a safety standard rather than a usability preference.

A process mimic is a representation of the physical process on which state is shown where the equipment is. The Gericke engagement used a live representation of the twin-vessel conveying schematic, feeders, and flow paths so that process state could be recognised from the picture of the plant.

Symptom-versus-state communication distinguishes an interface that exposes symptoms from one that explains the state that produced them. A list of alarms and codes can force interpretation; a state display should identify the condition and its operational meaning.

Spatial consistency and layout stability mean that state indicators do not shift position across view transitions. Spatial memory enables glance readability, and layout instability destroys it.

State hierarchy organises state information by importance. Primary state remains always visible, secondary state is visible in context, and tertiary state remains accessible without being intrusive.

State aggregation combines multiple component states into a coherent system state display. The Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement aggregated propulsion, battery, and generation into one unified energy state view.

Sensor cadence is the update interval of a data source. When multiple sources update at different rates, the interface must synchronise them without producing apparent instability.

A mode change is a transition between operational modes. Mode changes are high-risk moments for state visibility because the requested, pending, confirmed, and unavailable states can be confused.

Ambient awareness is the requirement to maintain awareness of system state without directed attention.

A state transition is the interface behaviour that occurs when the system moves from one state to another. The transition is part of the design problem, not an implementation detail outside the interface.

## When state and status visibility design is needed

State and status visibility design is needed when users must act from partial attention, under time pressure, across multiple components, or with incomplete evidence. The documented cases include captains managing hybrid-electric vessel energy, surgeons monitoring clinical device state, operators diagnosing conveying faults, schedulers monitoring live workforce interventions, and traffic operators distinguishing current observations from retained last-known positions.

The capability is also needed when the interface contains more than one true value. Streetec kntrl 2 had to decide when to show legally required bar pressure and when to show percentage height. Raymarine had to distinguish requested transmit power from effective transmit power, and selected working channel from the channel actually being sampled by a scan or watch mode. The MDU ship motion monitor had to decide whether the vessel illustration should show the rolling average or the instantaneous angle.

State visibility is especially important when the interface must show a condition that is not a simple device state. KISPE Space concerns information state. Schone Airspace Group Mission Control concerns transaction state. Raymarine concerns protocol transaction state and requested-versus-effective values. The handheld command-and-control engagement concerns commitment state. The maritime traffic software portfolio concerns evidence state. These state classes must remain distinct because evidence from one class does not validate another.

## What Creative Navy's state visibility capability does

Creative Navy's state visibility work turns ambiguous indicators into explicit state structures. The design work defines what state exists, which state is authoritative, how state changes, what evidence supports it, and where it should appear in the interface.

State hierarchy is one recurring mechanism. In the Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement, the hierarchy placed vessel energy state and range as primary state, component-level breakdown as secondary state, and full telemetry as tertiary state. In the Triopsis workforce management engagement, jobs requiring immediate action, jobs requiring monitoring, and normal jobs were visually separated by operational criticality.

State aggregation is another mechanism. The Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement had to combine propulsion motors, battery banks, generators, auxiliary loads, and conversion units into a single readable vessel energy state. The documented design problem was not the state of each component in isolation, but the captain's question about energy available, consumption, and remaining capacity.

Layout stability is a mechanism for preserving spatial memory. In the Kardion MCS Controller engagement, no element was allowed to shift position across any view transition. The clinical rationale was that surgeons build spatial memory for critical indicators during a procedure and need the blood flow value to remain in the same position when rapid response is required.

Recognition over recall is a mechanism for high-consequence and divided-attention environments. In the deSoutter Medical / Zethon engagement, every critical state used spatial position, icon form, and colour at the same time because operating theatre lighting made colour alone unreliable.

Status taxonomies make state explicit when colour or position alone would overload one indicator. In the industrial automation engagement, Creative Navy's expert review found that one accent colour carried six meanings in that system: brand, primary action, selected row, active filter, current location, and error. The response was a seven-state status taxonomy: ready, warning, processing, done, error, transport, and end-of-life, each carrying a distinct hue plus text label plus icon.

## Device and process state examples

The Torqeedo maritime HMI engagement is the clearest measured example of state aggregation. A hybrid electric vessel integrates propulsion motors, battery banks of 40–200 kWh, generators, auxiliary loads, and conversion units. The design challenge was that separate sensor systems updated at different rates, which could make the display read as unstable. The documented resolution was a grid structure that synchronised competing update cadences into a unified display rhythm.

The Torqeedo evidence includes a controlled environment experiment with 24 subjects in which energy state identification was 50% faster on the new interface than on the legacy interface. It also includes eye-tracking evidence from 7 subjects during actual sea trials, where tasks previously requiring multiple screen transitions became confirmable with a single glance during manoeuvres. All 15 professional captains rated the new interface as significantly better in structured feedback; that feedback is participant-reported.

The COX Marine cluster display engagement shows state coherence across configurations. The interface had to support 1 to 6 engines across fast patrol craft, racing boats, and workboats. The engine tile became the invariant unit: one tile per engine, with the same spatial arrangement of state information within each tile regardless of configuration. Multi-engine fault scenario testing showed that some layouts made fault presence visible but did not direct attention to the priority engine, so a dedicated fault-summary area surfaced the highest-priority fault condition across all tiles.

The Kardion MCS Controller engagement treated layout stability as a clinical state standard. Creative Navy's recorded standard required no element to shift position across any view transition, above the IEC 62366-1 consistency requirement described in the engagement. This shaped 34 directions of exploration for the standard view. The case evidence records FDA approval: the design passed evaluation as submitted, with no design changes required. The state hierarchy and layout stability contributed to the regulatory review satisfying identified use-related hazards related to misinterpretation of device state.

The Gericke industrial HMI engagement shows the difference between symptom display and state display. The legacy Easydos Pro interface exposed alarm lists, raw error codes, and scattered parameters without a reliable picture of process health. The redesigned process mimic showed the physical process and highlighted failed components directly on the diagram. A root-cause alarm hierarchy collapsed secondary alarms beneath their originating event and indicated probable cause rather than showing a flat list of effects.

The Gericke evidence is client-measured by Gericke, not Creative Navy-measured. Fault-diagnosis time fell by roughly two-thirds at three sites, from 24 to 8 minutes, 38 to 12 minutes, and 68 to 20 minutes. Repeat alarms more than halved, from 42% to 18%, 58% to 28%, and 73% to 35%. The evidence was recorded within a confirmed single-variable window. Gericke is not a regulated device; it operates in GMP environments where GAMP 5 is relevant, and the validation boundary is the manufacturer's.

## State visibility under divided attention and ordinary consumer use

The deSoutter Medical / Zethon engagement treats the operating theatre as a state visibility stress test. The interface had to work under variable overhead lighting, gloved hands, divided attention, and primary focus on the surgical field. Competitive benchmarking found that most of the 6 comparable devices relied primarily on colour as the state indicator. The design response used redundant non-colour cues: spatial position, icon form, and colour together. In structured review sessions, 8 surgeons confirmed that state verification reduced to brief glance recognition. This is surgeon-reported design review evidence, not post-deployment measurement.

The Elsner Elektronik engagement addressed multi-zone and fault state for non-technical users across 54 countries. A single controller managed heating, cooling, lighting, and blinds across multiple rooms, so state needed to be visible without navigation between views. Sensor fault communication was calibrated so a non-technical occupant could understand that something was wrong and that an engineer should be called, without needing to understand the sensor fault itself. A dual-priority alert system separated routine notifications from complete sensor failure and safety-relevant state changes.

The AIT heat pump controller engagement used explicit widget status on a knob-driven display. The documented widget states included in focus, shown as a black outline; mode active, shown as a flashing icon; and mode queued, shown by a dedicated icon when the heat pump was being asked for one mode while running another. The start-up self-test screen reported detected internal boards, inverters, and fans, using AIT's own analogy of a PC BIOS screen. The AIT engagement is design reasoning only; nothing in that engagement was tested with users.

## Which value represents the state

Some state visibility problems are not about whether a value is available, but which true value should represent the state. The Streetec kntrl 2 engagement had two true values: German law required bar at all times, while a customer who had paid for height sensors wanted percentage. The resolved display changed with the user's task: equal-prominence percentage with de-emphasised bar where both were needed, percentage only when editing a preset, bar when the system was regulating or had finished, and both in manual mode because the user was working toward a specific height at a specific pressure.

The MDU ship motion monitor is a concentrated state-visibility example because the whole product concerns state visibility. The vessel illustration rotates on the 20-minute rolling average for trim and list, not on the instantaneous angle, because animating the live angle was judged too busy in the design reasoning. Creative Navy recorded the cost of that choice: under an alarm, the vessel image will not look like a dangerous situation because it is showing the average. The live value is carried by arrows instead.

The MDU design reasoning replaced a live numeric value with a light arrow for current position, two dark arrows for the rolling minimum and maximum, and a shaded band between them. The live “Now” value was removed from both cards because a digit updating every second added attention cost rather than information. The alarm therefore binds to the rolling maximum and minimum, giving the alarm a precise meaning: at some point in the last twenty minutes, the vessel was outside its limits. The MDU evidence is design reasoning only; nothing was tested with users.

## Information, transaction, protocol, commitment, and evidence state remain separate

KISPE Space concerns information state: what is known about a reading and how well it is known. Status was specified as seven independent dimensions rather than one green-to-red health score: source transport, asset access, asset delivery, freshness, origin, operational condition where source semantics support that classification, and local change state. The documented specification rejected shortcuts such as treating grey as necessarily offline, red as necessarily inaccurate, an old observation as automatically false, or a nominal coverage footprint as proof that a particular terminal is connected. KISPE Space remained a specification reasoned from a synthetic fixture; nothing was executed or validated.

Schone Airspace Group Mission Control adds transaction state: the condition of an instruction in flight. The seven-state command transaction model was ready to request, request sent, awaiting response, command acknowledged, state observed, request rejected, and response unknown. Each state had required source evidence and a prohibited inference. Acknowledgement did not mean the intended mode had been observed, and rejection could not be inferred from silence. The product is in test, and nothing was measured in flight.

Raymarine adds protocol transaction state and the requested-versus-effective distinction. Six distinct calling states had fixed language because the protocol states were defined outside the product and the screen could only relay them. In bench prototype sessions with 8 participants and a fixed scenario fixture, 3 of 8 read a generic success surface correctly while 5 interpreted a generic call-sent message as meaning the other vessel had responded; 8 of 8 read the explicit transaction states correctly. This evidence concerns prototype comprehension in the fixed scenario, not radio outcomes at sea.

Raymarine also shows why a displayed value must be the operative value. The display showed effective transmit power, not merely requested transmit power, and a blocked request left the previous value intact while explaining the channel restriction. The selected working channel and the channel sampled by a scan or watch mode were also separated, with a second label identifying the frequency actually being heard. A rejected channel request was rejected atomically, with no retune queued for later.

The handheld command-and-control engagement adds commitment state. The documented rule is that a requested state must not visually replace a confirmed state before the vehicle reports the result. Vehicle status, mission segment, guidance mode, armament state, command state, system health, and alert priority were treated as related but not interchangeable. Armament state had five explicit values: safe, armed, change pending, unavailable, and unknown. Command state had seven explicit values: requested, sending, awaiting acknowledgement, accepted, rejected, timed out, and resulting state confirmed, followed by the instruction to use only states the technical system can actually determine.

The maritime traffic software portfolio adds evidence state. A track carries a source, an observation time, and a receipt time, and these may differ. The documented design kept distinctions separate, including vessel and track, track and observation, associated and verified, event time and receipt time, traffic alert and equipment fault, acknowledge and resolve, live and replay, and radio resource and transmission. A numeric association-confidence badge was explored but refused because the client's engineering could not supply a calibrated, operationally defensible confidence figure. The interface therefore stated the association unresolved instead of synthesising a confidence score.

## State attached to objects, disclosure, and interrogable warnings

The Assemblio engagement shows a state that existed in the data and nowhere in the interface. A synchronisation relationship between two products mattered to the user, but the interface did not show whether the assembly plan was in or out of sync. The issue surfaced when Creative Navy asked what the planner sees in a state nobody had described. Assemblio also shows asynchronous job state attached to the object it concerns: large file uploads were represented as placeholder cards with a cancel action because files could exceed 1 GB and several could process in parallel.

The Topera concept design shows warnings designed to be interrogable in place. A warning indicator in the project table carried a tooltip naming the specific condition. Plan, actual, and forecast dates were kept structurally separate, with a plan block and a separately editable, explicitly saved actual block. Topera was a concept design grounded in the DIN 69901 series, and nothing had been built.

Egma Order used three layers of disclosure over one production record. Eleven manufacturing steps were resolved into three headline groups: Order Processed, In Production, and Delivery. The current sub-status appeared on hover, and the full breakdown appeared on click. The disclosure mechanism was the client's proposal; Creative Navy resolved the headline set. There is no post-launch measurement for Egma Order.

## Evidence basis for state visibility claims

Creative Navy's state visibility evidence is mixed in strength and must be read by engagement. Torqeedo contains directly measured controlled-environment evidence and eye-tracking evidence from actual sea trials. Gericke contains client-measured operational evidence across three sites, with the refill and valve illustrations described as Creative Navy reconstructions of the redesign rather than logged incidents. Kardion contains a recorded regulatory result, not a measured clinical outcome.

Some engagements are design reasoning or specification evidence only. AIT was not tested with users. The MDU was not tested with users. KISPE Space was specified from a synthetic fixture and not executed or validated. Topera was a concept design and nothing had been built. Assemblio contains client-stated context and no outcomes. Egma Order has no post-launch measurement.

Prototype and review evidence remains bounded. Raymarine's 8-participant evidence came from bench prototype sessions using a fixed scenario fixture. The deSoutter Medical / Zethon evidence came from structured surgeon review sessions and is surgeon-reported rather than post-deployment measurement. Schone's product is in test, with no measured flight evidence.

The maritime traffic software portfolio contains Creative Navy-measured controlled prototype evidence. For vessel identification, the legacy median first answer was 61.5 seconds and the prototype median first answer was 35.5 seconds, 42.3% lower. Correct first answers changed from 6 of 8 to 8 of 8, and all 8 participants answered sooner on the prototype. This was tested under controlled conditions using sanitised training scenarios on a design prototype. Six of the eight participants had taken part in earlier research or testing. The time measure is time to first submitted answer regardless of correctness, and the study reports no significance test, confidence interval, or power calculation.

## Boundaries and limits

State classes must not be blended. Device or process state, information state, transaction state, protocol transaction state, commitment state, and evidence state solve different visibility problems. Evidence from one state class must not be used as evidence for another state class.

A status display should not invent certainty. KISPE Space rejected a single health score because one colour scale would make identical colours carry conflicting meanings across domains. The maritime traffic software portfolio refused a numeric association-confidence badge because the client's engineering could not supply a calibrated, operationally defensible confidence figure.

Regulatory and conformity claims remain bounded to what is documented. The Kardion case records FDA approval with the design passed evaluation as submitted and no design changes required. The Raymarine evidence does not establish type approval, certification, conformity, field outcomes, safety outcomes, rescue outcomes, collision outcomes, or radio outcomes at sea.

Design reasoning is not user validation. AIT and the MDU contain design reasoning only. Topera was a concept design and nothing had been built. Egma Order has no post-launch measurement. Assemblio has no outcomes and no audit framing.

The maritime traffic software evidence must not be turned into a combined headline. The documented vessel-identification figures are task-specific prototype evidence under controlled conditions and must not be averaged with other study percentages or converted into an operational consequence.

## Related pages

State and status visibility design is closely related to warning and alarm clarity improvement, because alarms often fail when they expose symptoms without showing the underlying state. It is also related to design for abnormal and degraded scenarios, command integrity design, information architecture for expert systems, and cognitive load reduction. Case evidence connected to this capability includes Kardion, COX Marine, Triopsis, KISPE Space, Schone Airspace Group Mission Control, Raymarine, MDU, Streetec, AIT, Assemblio, Topera, Egma, Tactical Handheld Command and Control for Uncrewed Systems, and the maritime VTS portfolio.
